served.stem: In a Gabriel synthesis using potassium phthalimide (shown) followed by hydrazinolysis, which alkyl halide will give the highest yield of the desired primary amine?
served.bankWhy: The phthalimide anion alkylates via SN2, so it needs an unhindered substrate; 1-bromobutane (primary) gives the best yield. Tertiary halides undergo E2 elimination, and aryl/vinyl halides are unreactive toward SN2.

answer.line: The phthalimide nitrogen alkylates by SN2, and SN2 wants an open back side on an sp3 carbon. A primary halide is the best fit.

steps: Name the step that decides it: the phthalimide anion attacks the halide's carbon by SN2.
SN2 needs a back side to come in from: tertiary is walled off, and an sp2 carbon on a ring or a C=C has none it can use. Primary is open.
Hydrazine then frees the amine, so 1-bromobutane gives butan-1-amine. Phthalimide attacks once and is boxed in, so it never alkylates twice.

choices.note: Primary, sp3, unhindered: the substrate SN2 wants.
Bromide leaves well, which is the pull. But an aryl C-Br sits on an sp2 carbon whose back side is inside the ring, so no SN2.
Tertiary is the best SN1 substrate and the worst SN2 one. With the basic phthalimide anion it eliminates instead.
Three methyls block the back side, so SN2 cannot happen. The anion acts as a base and E2 gives isobutylene.
Same story as the aryl halide: the C-Br is on an sp2 carbon, the bond is strong, and the pi system blocks the back side.

student.lockIt: The Gabriel synthesis runs on SN2: use a primary alkyl halide, never tertiary, aryl or vinyl.
